gate-blindspots.title: The served page (GET /) is structurally invisible - dropped by the trailing-slash trim AND excluded from the unprobed confession
gate-blindspots.evidence: swarm.rs:18990 `raw.trim_end_matches([';', ',', ')', '.', '/'])` turns the path token `/` into an empty string, and 18991 `if path.is_empty() { continue; }` drops it; the table-merge path repeats the same trim at 19028-19030. Meanwhile spec_unprobed_advertised's trim set at 19071-19072 does NOT include '/', so probeable_get_path("/") returns Some("/") at 19069-19077 and the row is skipped from the unprobed list as 'probeable'. The root page is neither probed nor named as unprobed - doubly silent.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: An app that 404s on /, serves an empty shell, or ships no frontend at all passes the gate green with verified>0 from its API GETs. This is a Tier-A defect in the scorer: score_build.py:350 serves_page (A) fails it immediately, and the entire ui_states/ui_currency/ui_offline/ui_polish family (score_build.py:469, 478, 487, 745) plus every V/J product check goes to zero on a build the gate declared clean.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Special-case the root path: after the trim, restore '' to '/' (or exempt a bare '/' token from the trailing-slash trim - the trim exists to kill the F32 backtick phantom '/`.', not the legitimate root). Probe it, assert 200 and that the body contains '<' (the exact serves_page predicate). Also make spec_unprobed_advertised's trim consistent so a dropped root is at least confessed.

gate-blindspots.title: GET bodies are asserted for key PRESENCE only - documented VALUES are parsed by spec_advertised_surface and then discarded
gate-blindspots.evidence: spec_documented_keys (swarm.rs:18875-18906) extracts only key NAMES via the regex `"(\w+)"\s*:` ; the consuming loop at 19381-19401 checks `v.get(k).is_none()` - existence, nothing else. The spec's EXPECT cell IS captured by spec_advertised_surface at swarm.rs:3619-3624 (`-> EXPECT {expected}`) but every consumer (spec_get_endpoints 19019-19040, spec_post_endpoints 3631-3643) splits off method+path and throws the expected shape away. The only value assertions in the whole gate are the UTC designator (19404-19416) and the post-sync total==0 check.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: An app serving {"status": "error", "payments": -1, "last_sync": "never"} on /api/health, or a summary whose total_minor is any wrong integer, has every documented key present and increments `verified`. The scorer later fails it across health_semantics (score_build.py:664 - asserts status=='ok', fresh-boot zero, post-sync count), summary_accuracy (:432 - compares total_minor to EXPECTED_SUM), total_field (:412) and chronological_order (:419).
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Use the EXPECT cell the parser already extracts: when the cell carries a concrete literal ("status": "ok"), assert the value; when it carries a typed placeholder (<int>), assert the JSON type. Both are spec-derived and deterministic, same fail-open discipline as spec_documented_keys (prose cell => assert nothing).

gate-blindspots.title: Restart/persistence is invisible - one process lifetime, one fresh scratch DB, child killed at the end
gate-blindspots.evidence: run_spec_contract spawns python3 exactly once (swarm.rs:19252-19262) on a per-invocation scratch DB (19233-19239) and kills it at 19593 after all probes. Nothing ever restarts the process and re-reads the GETs. The sync POST, the persistence-through-GET check (19559-19590) and every body assertion all execute inside the same process lifetime.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: A store that is 'memory dressed as a database' (the scorer's own words) - an in-process dict behind a --db flag that never touches the file - passes every arm: sync reports counts, GET total reads non-zero, idempotency holds. score_build.py:559 restart_persistence (C) SIGKILLs and reboots on the same --db and catches exactly this; the gate structurally cannot.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: After a POST that reported acquired>0 and a GET that read total>0, kill the child, respawn with the identical advertised argv and the SAME scratch DB, and re-read the total-carrying GET. total dropping to 0 across the restart is an unambiguous finding; failure to rebind stays a finding via the existing advertised-argv never-bound arm (19337-19343).

gate-blindspots.title: Rendered UI is unreachable in principle - the gate is curl-only, no DOM, no JS execution, no console
gate-blindspots.evidence: Every probe in run_spec_contract is a tokio::process curl (swarm.rs:19354, 19466, 19566). There is no browser, no HTML parse, and even the non-JSON branch at 19418-19422 only fires when a JSON shape was documented - an HTML body is fail-open by design (18873: 'a row whose response cell is prose or an HTML page must not invent a check').
gate-blindspots.mechanism: A page whose JS throws on load, renders no rows, shows raw minor units, or never wires the Sync button ships green. The sb-5 product tier grades exactly this and the gate cannot see any of it: J-family j_loads_data/j_console_clean/j_sync_journey/j_error_state/j_empty_state (score_build.py:1090-1157) and V-family v_dates_readable/v_status_distinct/v_pagination/v_filter/v_responsive_375/v_styling (:1180-1285) all run through product_probe.mjs in a real browser. Per the PRODUCT-TIER commit (785e9a4e2) a gate-side render is already the planned sb-5 boundary work.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: The planned gate-side render: a headless page-load of GET / that asserts the DOM claims a row count matching the API total (the browser-truth probe pattern from commit 6df0c2b76) and that the console is exception-free. Short of that, the gate should at minimum stop counting a build 'verified' when the spec advertises a page it never opened.

gate-blindspots.title: Zero-only persistence check plus untrusted-claim trust: partial sync (3 of 247 rows) passes, and vendor_truth_total is never compared to what the app SERVES
gate-blindspots.evidence: The persistence-through-GET check fires only on `reads_zero` - max of total/count `== Some(0)` (swarm.rs:19575-19579). The acquired count comes from the app's OWN response via post_reports_acquired (19559, defined 18952-18959) and is never cross-checked. vendor_truth_total (18806-18829) is fetched (19443) but consumed only by the Vacuous arm (19519-19529) - it is never compared against the GET's served total.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: An app that claims fetched=247 but persists one page (total=25), or truncates to 3 rows, passes: 25 != 0, no duplicate, no growth. F825 closed only the total==0 corner. The scorer grades the fraction: sync_completeness (score_build.py:370, got/EXPECTED_TOTAL) and total_field (:412, exact 247) both fail it later.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: The ground truth is already in scope: when vendor_total is Some((n,_)) with n>0, compare the total-carrying GET's served value against n after the first POST - a served total materially below the vendor's is a completeness finding, not just total==0. Same fail-open ladder as F825 (no vendor => today's behavior).

gate-blindspots.title: Error-path contracts are never exercised - the gate only ever sends valid requests, and non-404/405 4xx is fail-open
gate-blindspots.evidence: The GET loop's status ladder (swarm.rs:19369-19426) treats 5xx and 404/405 as findings, 2xx as verified, and everything else fail-open ('3xx / other 4xx (a route that needs a body/auth) -> neither a finding nor verified', 19426). No probe anywhere sends an invalid limit, a garbage offset, or a malformed body; templated query params are filled with the benign literal 1 (18859).
gate-blindspots.mechanism: An app that 500s on ?limit=abc, returns an HTML traceback page on a bad offset, or accepts garbage silently ships green. The scorer exercises a 7-cell invalid-input matrix - input_validation (score_build.py:455, half status + half the documented error body) - and json_everywhere (:645) grades error responses for JSON parse + content-type; both are outside the gate's reach today.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Add a deterministic error-probe arm to the GET loop: for each templated query param, re-issue with a non-numeric value and assert the response is 4xx (not 5xx) and parses as JSON. Both properties are generic (the spec's 'every response is JSON' sentence), need no vendor, and reuse the existing curl plumbing.

gate-blindspots.title: Query templates are filled but their semantics are never asserted - limit=1 is sent, the response length is never checked
gate-blindspots.evidence: probeable_get_path fills a templated value with the literal 1 (swarm.rs:18857-18859) so /api/payments?limit=1&offset=1 IS probed - but the consuming loop (19352-19425) asserts only status, documented-key presence, and UTC. Nothing compares len(data) to the limit it just sent, or the echoed limit/offset fields to the request.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: An app that ignores limit and offset entirely and dumps all 247 rows on every request answers 200 with data/total/limit/offset all present - verified. score_build.py:390 local_pagination (B) checks default-25/cap-100/offset slicing and fails it; uses_max_limit (:700) and request_efficiency (:682) grade the client side of the same contract.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: When the probe filled `limit=1`, assert the returned data array (a documented key on that row) has length <= 1, and if the shape echoes `limit`, that it echoes the value sent. Purely derived from what the gate itself already constructed - no new spec parsing.

gate-blindspots.title: The whole mutating arm - including F825 vendor truth and persistence-through-GET - is behind a default-OFF env gate
gate-blindspots.evidence: swarm.rs:19439 `if swarm_gate("GOOSE_SWARM_PROBE_ADVERTISED_POST", false)` wraps vendor_truth_total (19443), both POST calls, repeated_post_verdict, the Vacuous->finding upgrade, and the acquired-but-not-persisted check (19559-19590). With the gate unset the contract check is bare GETs, and the green decision at 29957 is findings.is_empty() - `verified` narrows the claim (29974) but never blocks green.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: In the default configuration every defect class the POST arm was built from re-opens: zero-acquisition syncs (F823's measured 0/247 green), duplicating re-syncs, non-cheap re-downloads, and store/API disconnects all pass. Scorer families sync_completeness (:370), resync_idempotent (:378), second_sync_cost (:707) and update_propagation (:545) carry them.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Once the write-probe has enough clean mileage, flip the default on (or fold it into spec_contract_enabled) so the arm's absence is a deliberate opt-out rather than the silent baseline; the probed_post counter (29867) already exists to make the OFF state measurable.

gate-blindspots.title: Param'd-path routes are excluded from probing, and the unprobed confession is suppressed whenever any POST was probed
gate-blindspots.evidence: probeable_get_path returns None for any base containing {, <, : (swarm.rs:18847), so GET /api/payments/{id} is never curled - correct in itself - but the naming compensator is conditionally disabled: swarm.rs:19597-19601 `let unprobed = if post_probed > 0 { Vec::new() } else { spec_unprobed_advertised(spec) };` drops the ENTIRE unprobed list (param'd GETs, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) the moment one POST is probed.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: With POST probing on, a spec advertising GET /api/payments/{id} that 500s on every real id produces no finding AND no inconclusive naming the omission - the exact silent-drop shape spec_unprobed_advertised's own doc comment (19044-19057) says it exists to prevent. The scorer's row-level families (payment_row_shape :402, row_integrity :598) read the collection instead and would surface the data, but a per-item endpoint defect has no gate-side witness at all.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Make the suppression subtractive, not total: filter spec_unprobed_advertised to remove only the POST paths actually probed (spec_post_endpoints intersect probed) instead of clearing the list. One-line change at 19597.

gate-blindspots.title: Perf is invisible - the only clocks are failure timeouts, no latency is measured or reported
gate-blindspots.evidence: GET probes run curl -m 5 (swarm.rs:19360), POSTs -m 20 (19467), smoke_output adds outer caps of 8/25s - all pass/fail cliffs. No elapsed time is captured, compared to a budget, or emitted in the spec_contract event (29854-29904 carries only counts and reasons).
gate-blindspots.mechanism: A list endpoint taking 4.9 seconds or a sync taking 19 seconds sails through indistinguishable from a 20ms one. The sb-5 P family grades exactly this - p_list_latency, p_page_interactive, p_sync_wall (score_build.py:1158-1179) via graded _ladder budgets - and the gate structurally cannot see any of it today.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Record wall-clock per probe (Instant::elapsed around the existing smoke_output calls) and emit it in the spec_contract event; even without a hard budget, a graphed latency makes the perf axis ablatable, and a spec-stated budget line could later upgrade it to a finding.

gate-blindspots.title: Update propagation is out of reach - the gate cannot mutate the vendor, so an INSERT-only sync is invisible
gate-blindspots.evidence: The POST arm issues two identical bare POSTs (swarm.rs:19465-19478) against an unchanged vendor; repeated_post_verdict (3705-3784) can only decide duplicate/cheap/vacuous from the two response bodies. There is no third sync after a vendor-side change, and vendor_truth_total (18806) only reads a count.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: A sync that upserts by INSERT OR IGNORE - never updating an existing row's status - is perfectly idempotent and cheap by every body the gate reads, yet shows stale statuses forever. score_build.py:545 update_propagation (C) mutates 25 vendor statuses and requires sync3 to bring them home; that needs vendor-mutation access the gate does not have and arguably should not grow.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Accept as a scorer-only family, but say so: add the omission to the gate's inconclusive confession (the spec_unprobed_advertised pattern) so 'propagation unverified by the gate' is stated rather than assumed.

gate-blindspots.title: Concurrency is never exercised - every probe in the gate is sequential
gate-blindspots.evidence: The two POSTs are awaited one after the other (swarm.rs:19470-19473), the GET loop is a serial for-loop (19352), and the post-acquisition GET re-probes are serial too (19560-19589). No two requests are ever in flight against the app at once.
gate-blindspots.mechanism: The measured cross-thread sqlite failure class (named in the F753 comment at 19553-19558) only detonates under overlapping requests - two operators pressing Sync at once duplicating or losing rows. The gate cannot trigger it; score_build.py:730 concurrent_sync_safe (D) fires two overlapping syncs and asserts total==EXPECTED_TOTAL.
gate-blindspots.fix_direction: Cheap gate-side version: issue the two idempotency POSTs concurrently (join! instead of sequential awaits) on a third call pair, then assert the total-carrying GET matches the pre-concurrency value. Reuses every helper already present; a growth or 5xx under overlap is an unambiguous finding.

n3-r0.title: Judge is a 62x rubber stamp: 59/59 LLM verdicts 'ok' at confidence 1.0, zero hints/nudges/kills; only the 3 deterministic staleness-accepts did anything
n3-r0.evidence: 62 judge_observed -> 62 judge_verdict: verdicts {ok: 59, accept: 3}, actions {observed: 59, accepted: 3}, confidence 1.0 on all 62, hint empty on all 59 'ok' rows, deterministic=false on all 59. Only 9 of the 59 non-deterministic verdicts even carry a judge_node; 50 have judge_node="". Plus 50 judge_skipped, every one reason='no_idle_device' (24 in 02:40-02:49 alone). The judge watched task 'cli' across 8 observations while secs_since_last_write climbed 40 -> 134 -> 207 -> 269 -> 337 -> 399 -> 505 -> 589 and said 'ok' every time; the deterministic accept at 02:49:27 (seq 132) is what finally freed the device. The 3 accepts (cli seq 132, test-cli seq 262, integrate-verify seq 268) are the judge's only non-trivial output in 62 verdicts.
n3-r0.mechanism: The LLM verdict path never produces anything but 'ok' (judge_nudge lever is false in levers_resolved, so it cannot intervene), and 45% of its cycles (50/112) are starved because it needs an idle device. All actual value came from the deterministic file-staleness accepter, which needs no LLM at all.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Either enable judge_nudge so the observe path can act on the staleness it is already measuring, or drop the LLM verdict call entirely and keep only the deterministic accepter (cheaper, and it is the only component that acted this run) — with a much lower staleness threshold, since the accept criterion (owned file exists + syntax pass + stale) was observably satisfied ~9 minutes before it fired for 'cli'.

n3-r0.title: ~24.5 min of device time burned holding finished/stalled tasks: cli stale 589s, test-cli stale 879s including a 441s retry that did literally nothing
n3-r0.evidence: 'cli' (mac-gabee): dispatched 02:38:05, last owned-file write ~02:39:38 (secs_since_write=40 at 02:40:18), accepted 02:49:27 with hint 'nothing has changed for 589s' — 8 tool calls total, thinking_chars grew 1089 -> 8469 with no further writes (rumination). 'test-cli' (mac-gabee): attempt 0 dispatched 02:49:27, thinking_chars froze at 513 from 02:53:27 onward (dead session); task_retry fired 03:00:21 'agent stalled — no progress for 420s'; attempt 1 was re-dispatched to the SAME device (from_device == dispatch device mac-gabee), made 0 tool calls and froze at thinking_chars=257 from 03:02:06 to 03:07:42, when the deterministic accept fired on the attempt-0 file at 879s staleness. The stall detector never fired for attempt 1 despite 336+s of zero activity. Combined dead hold: 589 + 879 = 1468s on one device out of a ~1904s execute window x 3 devices.
n3-r0.mechanism: Two distinct stall shapes — token-generating rumination after the deliverable is done (cli) and a dead session (test-cli) — and neither is handled early: the staleness-accept threshold is minutes-deep, and the retry path re-lands on the very device that just stalled, where it stalls again below the 420s detector horizon.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Accept on (file exists + syntax pass + short staleness) far earlier; route retries to a different device than from_device; arm the stall detector for retry attempts from dispatch (attempt 1 had zero token/tool activity for its whole life and was never flagged).

n3-r0.title: pre_review found findings on 3 tasks and nothing ever consumed them: 0 fix tasks dispatched, final review reports zero; 39 min of fleet time spent producing discarded output
n3-r0.evidence: 10 pre_review events totalling 2345.9s of device time. had_findings=true for api (03:04:58, 170.7s), meridian (03:05:28, 401.7s), test-meridian (03:06:57, 456.4s). No fix task appears anywhere in the 22 dispatches; the review event at 03:09:49 reports findings: [], new_findings: [], pre_existing_skipped: 0; complete_result reports remaining_findings=0. levers_resolved shows fix_sched: false. Additionally the pre_review of test-cli completed at 03:10:36 — 47s AFTER complete_result and review (03:09:49) — structurally unable to influence anything.
n3-r0.mechanism: Pre-review runs and finds problems, but with fix_sched=false there is no consumer: the findings are neither turned into fix tasks nor carried into the final review or the completion gate, and one pre_review is even scheduled past the gate it could have informed.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Wire pre_review findings into fix scheduling (or into the complete_verify finding list) — or stop running pre_review at all; at 2346s it cost ~25% of the 3-device execute-phase budget for output the run then threw away. Also order pre_reviews to finish before the completion gate.

n3-r0.title: The completion gate passed while proving nothing: pytest couldn't bind its port (harness collision), the only POST endpoint was never probed, and complete_result says verified=false
n3-r0.evidence: complete_verify round 0 (03:09:49): passed=true, findings=0, but inconclusive_reasons include 'pytest -q could not bind a port (Address already in use) — another task in this run was serving the app at the same time... nothing was proven either way'. spec_contract round 0: verified=3, inconclusive=1, probed_post=0 — 'POST /api/sync ... NOT probed because this check only issues bare GETs'. complete_result: passed=true, verified=false, remaining_findings=0. run_finished phases: gates_min=0.0. Only one verify round ran (complete_cap_lifted allowed rounds=2, effective_secs=3000). The bench verdict then scored tier B at 0.3802 with sync_completeness 0/247 — exactly the surface the gate never exercised.
n3-r0.mechanism: The gate treats inconclusive as pass-through: a port collision caused by the run's own concurrent tasks silently voids the pytest leg, and the spec probe is GET-only, so the single mutating endpoint — the one whose downstream state all the tier-B checks read — exits the run untested and green.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Retry pytest on a free/ephemeral port instead of skipping; teach spec_contract to probe advertised POSTs (or at least fail-closed on probed_post=0 when the spec advertises one); treat 'passed but verified=false with inconclusive legs' as grounds for the second verify round the cap already budgeted.

n3-r0.title: 36.5% of wall clock elapsed before the first task dispatched, including 6.6 min of 'research' by scouts that had no research tools
n3-r0.evidence: run_started 02:19:55; first task_dispatched 02:38:05 — 1090s. research_tools: available=[], can_look_things_up=false, yet the scout phase ran 02:19:55 -> 02:26:31 (396s) to produce 3 findings. skeleton_drafts 267s; 10 detail_completed 02:33:03 -> 02:36:22 (sum 1550s, every one well under its 420s budget); then a 103s gap from last detail (02:36:22) to contracts/plan_loaded (02:38:05). run_finished confirms: research 6.6 + planning 11.6 = 18.2 of 49.9 total min. Also plan_loaded: plan_confidence=100 via 'pool-invariant: 68 -> 100 on a 1-node footing' (raw agreement_conf=68, pool_penalty=32), clearing ask_floor=85 — so ask_max_q=3 went unused.
n3-r0.mechanism: The planning ladder runs every rung serially at full length even when its own signals say it's cheap: scouts run with zero lookup capability (pure model recall against a spec that names a live docs URL), and the pool-invariant lifts a 68 agreement to a 100 confidence, guaranteeing the clarify step never triggers regardless of ask_floor.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Skip or drastically cap the scout phase when can_look_things_up=false (or give scouts the shell/fetch access workers demonstrably had — fetched_external=true appears in later task tool calls); close the 103s post-detail gap; re-examine whether the pool-invariant lift should be allowed to carry a plan across the ask_floor it would otherwise fail.

n3-r0.title: The meridian module's contract failed to parse and was silently dropped from injection while contracts were declared frozen
n3-r0.evidence: contracts event (02:38:05, seq 18): modules=4, frozen=true, injected=3, injected_modules=['cli','store','api']; validated shows meridian: bytes=759, parsed=false, error='invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?', public=[]. Meridian is the largest detailed task of the run (spec_chars=6244, detail took 275s) and its pre_review later flagged findings (had_findings=true, 03:05:28) that went nowhere.
n3-r0.mechanism: Contract validation detects the broken contract but the pipeline proceeds frozen anyway, so the one module too complex to produce a parseable contract is exactly the one that executes without any injected interface contract — the sibling modules build against nothing for it.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Fail-closed or regenerate on parsed=false before freezing: one repair round for an invalid module contract (the error is a syntax-level fix), or at minimum flag the run so downstream verify prioritizes the contract-less module.

n3-r0.title: The last 9.5 min of the run is a single-device sink/join tail, ending with a judge-salvaged integrate-verify and an unverified run command
n3-r0.evidence: From 03:01:36 only integrate-verify (workhorse) plus the dead test-cli retry are running; from 03:07:42 integrate-verify alone. integrate-verify: sink_plan cap 3215s; made 16 tool calls by 03:08:49, then no new actions, and was deterministically accepted at 03:09:49 ('owns no files, has taken 16 action(s), and has done nothing new for a while') after 493s. local-mihai idle from 03:06:57, gabee from 03:07:42. Then run_overview took 03:09:49 -> 03:11:07 (78s) with run_command_verified=false. Tail 03:01:36 -> 03:11:07 = 571s = 18.6% of the 3071s wall at <=1 productive device.
n3-r0.mechanism: The join is structurally serial (one sink task on one device) and the sink itself stalled after 16 actions, so a third of its 493s was staleness waiting for the accepter; the closing overview then spends 78s generating a run command it never verifies.
n3-r0.fix_direction: Give the idle devices tail work (e.g. the pre_reviews that instead ran during peak, or the never-attempted second verify round); apply the same tighter staleness-accept to the sink; actually execute the overview's run_command since two devices are idle at that point.

n3-r0.title: Completion telemetry contradicts judge telemetry for every judge-accepted task: tool_calls=[], salvaged=false, and elapsed_ms that drops the first attempt
n3-r0.evidence: task_completed for cli, test-cli, integrate-verify all report tool_calls=[] — but judge_observed recorded tool_calls=8 for cli (02:49:27), 2 for test-cli attempt 0, and 16 for integrate-verify (03:09:49). All 21 completions report salvaged=false even though these 3 tasks were closed by deterministic judge-accepts of stale sessions. test-cli's completion says attempts=2, elapsed_ms=440784 (attempt 1 only) while wall time from first dispatch was 1095s; session_id=null on that record.
n3-r0.mechanism: The judge-accept completion path constructs the task_completed record without the worker session's tool trace or a salvaged marker, and stamps elapsed from the current attempt only — so exactly the runs most in need of post-hoc diagnosis (stall salvages) are the ones whose completion records claim zero activity and normal completion.
n3-r0.fix_direction: On judge-accept, populate task_completed from the observed session (tool count, both attempts' elapsed) and set salvaged=true (or a distinct 'accepted_stale' status) so downstream analysis can separate real completions from reclaimed stalls.

n1-r0.title: Judge is 100% dead weight on the 1-node arm: 62/62 evaluations skipped, 62 rubber-stamp 'ok' verdicts, zero actions
n1-r0.evidence: Event census: judge_observed=62, judge_skipped=62 (every reason='no_idle_device'), judge_verdict=62 — all verdict='ok', action='observed', confidence=1.0, deterministic=false, hint=''. Zero judge_nudge, zero kills, zero splits across the whole run (03:29:54 first observation → 04:16:33 last). Meanwhile the judge OBSERVED stall-shaped windows it could not act on: task 'api' at elapsed 90s/150s had 0 tool calls and no owned file written (first write only after ~264s, seq 20/29/32); task 'web' reached secs_since_last_write=392 at elapsed 580s (seq 134); 'test-python-modules' reached secs_since_last_write=223 with tool_calls frozen at 13 and thinking_chars frozen at 6891 across 3 consecutive observations 03:59:33→04:01:43 (seq 176/182/185).
n1-r0.mechanism: In swarm.rs (~line 20728), the scheduler hands the judge a model only when a device has in_flight < weight; on this pool (1 device, weight 2, occupancy at depth-2 for 2738s of the 2905s execution window) judge_model_id is always empty, so every invocation returns JudgeOutcome::ok() via the no_idle_device branch — the semantic review, the M3 split proposal (which sits BELOW that early return), and any corrective hint are structurally unreachable, not declined. The skip path still stamps confidence=1.0 on a judgment that never ran. The judge_nudge lever was additionally false in levers_resolved.
n1-r0.fix_direction: On saturated pools, either give the judge a real path to act (reserve a supervision slot after N consecutive no_idle_device skips, or run the semantic review between worker turns at low priority) or stop running the observation loop at all on 1-node arms; independently, a skipped evaluation must not emit confidence=1.0 'ok' — emit verdict='unreviewed'/confidence=null so 62 skips can never be read downstream as 62 passing assessments.

n1-r0.title: Verify/fix loop never engaged and abstained on exactly the surface that cost the score: 0 findings, POST never probed, verified=false end to end
n1-r0.evidence: complete_cap_lifted granted rounds=2, effective_secs=3000, fix_cap_secs=1200 — but only one complete_verify fired (round=0, findings=0, passed=true) and zero complete_fix_dispatched/complete_fix_completed events exist. The battery: cross_module_drift checked=10 findings=0; http_timeout_scan checked=5, skipped_tests=5 (all 5 test files excluded by design), findings=0; spec_contract verified=3, probed_post=0, inconclusive=1 with reason 'this check only issues bare GETs: POST /api/sync ... not coverage of the advertised surface'; review modules=10 findings=[]. Result chain: complete_result{passed:true, verified:false}, run_overview run_command_verified=false. The run's OWN research brief (research_completed at +272s, edge-cases lens, grounded=true) explicitly recorded 'Conditional GET: responses carry ETag; send back as If-None-Match; 304 Not Modified' and the POST idempotency contract — yet no verify probe ever exercised either.
n1-r0.mechanism: spec_contract structurally issues bare GETs only, so the one advertised POST endpoint (/api/sync — the surface family where the already-diagnosed headline defect lives) is unprobeable; the single inconclusive it emits is what sets final_verified=false (swarm.rs:29974, verdict.established()), which then falsifies run_command_verified. With 0 findings the 2-round/3000s fix budget can never be entered, so the loop's repair capacity is keyed to a detector that cannot see the riskiest surface. Research findings flow into worker briefs but never become verify probes — the pipeline drops the run's own knowledge at the gate.
n1-r0.fix_direction: Add a POST prober to spec_contract (idempotent POST against a scratch DB copy, or POST+rollback using the API's own Idempotency-Key semantics), and compile golden checks from grounded research findings (the ETag/304 and idempotency facts were machine-readable in finding_texts) so the verify battery covers what the run itself documented; also include test files in http_timeout_scan or record their exclusion as inconclusive rather than findings=0/partial=false.

n1-r0.title: Serial planning head consumed 1028s — 25.7% of the 4009s wall — while completed task details sat undispatched for up to ~470s
n1-r0.evidence: run_started 03:11:16.572, first task_dispatched 03:28:24 (+1028.4s). Breakdown from event timestamps: research scouts 0→272.0s; skeleton_drafts 272→442.4s (secs=170); detail phase 442→903.2s (7 detail_completed, 2-wide, actual secs 61–233 vs budget 420 each); then a 125.2s gap from last detail_completed (+903.2) to contracts/plan_loaded (+1028.4). The 'meridian' detail was finished at +556.4s but meridian was dispatched at +1148s (03:30:24); 'cli' detail done at +751.3s, dispatched at +1028s. Tail adds 75.7s (last task_completed 04:16:50 → run_finished 04:18:05.7, of which the run_overview generation call is ~69s, 04:16:56.7→04:18:05.7).
n1-r0.mechanism: Dispatch is gated on the fully assembled plan (contracts + plan_loaded fire together at +1028.4) even though per-task specs stream out of the detail phase one by one; on a 1-node pool the planner is the same device, so the entire head is dead execution time — no worker ran for the first 17.1 minutes.
n1-r0.fix_direction: Stream-dispatch: release a task to a free slot as soon as its detail_completed lands and its deps' contracts are frozen (the four implementer contracts were already validated per-module), instead of barriering on the whole plan; the first two details were ready at +556/+604, worth ~7 minutes of the head on this run.

n1-r0.title: One fat test task monopolized half the execution window (1523s) and serialized the 'parallel' e2e shards; the split machinery that exists for exactly this is behind the unreachable judge gate
n1-r0.evidence: test-python-modules: elapsed_ms=1,523,000 (25.4 min) = 52.4% of the 2905s execution window and 38% of wall, dispatched 03:41:34, completed 04:06:57, 22 tool calls, judged 24 times — every verdict the skipped default. While it held one of the two slots, verify-e2e::0 (03:54:48→04:00:13, 324.8s) and verify-e2e::1 (04:00:13→04:07:57, 464.9s) — whose descriptions both say 'runs in PARALLEL with its sibling shards' and whose deps were identical and satisfied at 03:54:48 — ran strictly serially, 789.7s combined for two boots of the same app. Levers: split=true, but 0 split actions and 0 join_spliced events.
n1-r0.mechanism: The M3 is_split_candidate/propose_split path in swarm.rs sits AFTER the `judge_model_id.is_empty()` early return, so on a saturated 1-node pool a fat task can never be partitioned — the 62/62 no_idle_device skips prove the branch was never reachable. The plan also authored one task owning all three Python test files (test_meridian.py, test_store.py, test_api.py) despite parallel_tests=true, guaranteeing a long pole.
n1-r0.fix_direction: Partition test authorship at plan time (one task per test file — the ownership split already exists in the plan data), and/or move the split decision to a deterministic scheduler check (task age × owned-file count) that does not require an idle judge device; e2e shards should preempt or interleave rather than queue behind a test-author task when their deps are green.

n1-r0.title: The entire plan-quality ladder no-oped: best-of-2 skeletons clamped to 1, plan_confidence null, converge/retarget levers had no input
n1-r0.evidence: skeleton_drafts: requested_best_of_n=2 but requested=1, clamped=true, distinct_draft_models=1, secs=170. plan_loaded: plan_confidence=null (ask_floor=85). Levers on with nothing to consume: converge=true, retarget=true with retarget_rounds=4, backbone=true — yet 0 plan_convergence, 0 confidence_retarget, 0 confidence_rescored, 0 retarget_discarded, 0 low_confidence_ask events fired in the whole run.
n1-r0.mechanism: Draft count is capped by DISTINCT MODEL NAMES, not devices or slots (n = requested_n.min(draft_models.len()), swarm.rs ~:14142); a homogeneous 1-node pool has one distinct model, so exactly one skeleton is drafted, cross-draft agreement cannot be computed, and every confidence-gated mechanism downstream (ask floor, retarget rounds, convergence) is inputless — the run pays the 170s skeleton cost and gets none of the selection value. Source comments confirm plan_confidence NULL in 11/11 one-node runs; this run is the 12th.
n1-r0.fix_direction: Let a single model produce N drafts with decorrelation (draft_temp lever exists and is null; temperature/top_p jitter or distinct seeds) so 1-node arms get an agreement signal, or explicitly log the ladder as disabled instead of silently carrying dead levers.

n1-r0.title: Read-only verify:: micro-shards spent 623.7s of worker sessions on checks that were 1 shell call each in the worst cases
n1-r0.evidence: Five verify:: tasks totaled 623.7s of the 2905s execution window (21.5%): verify::cli 78.8s (7 shell calls), verify::meridian 68.7s (1 shell call), verify::store 45.2s (1 shell call), verify::api 177.3s (4 calls), verify::web 253.7s (9 calls). verify::meridian and verify::store each ran a full 27B-model session — ~1000-char prompt, ~2000 thinking chars observed — to execute a single import/build-check command.
n1-r0.mechanism: fan_verify=true dispatches every per-module import gate as a complete LLM worker task; on a 2-slot pool each such session displaces real work, and for trivial modules the model contributes nothing beyond invoking one interpreter command the engine could run itself (the engine already owns deterministic gates — run_smoke_gate — for exactly this class of check).
n1-r0.fix_direction: Run the per-module import/build check deterministically in the engine (extend run_smoke_gate per-module) and reserve LLM verify shards for modules where the check needs judgment; on small pools this returns ~10 min of slot time per run.

n1-r0.title: Counter inconsistency: 'worker_count' means device count in pool_resolved (1) but slot count in skeleton_drafts (2)
n1-r0.evidence: pool_resolved: {devices:[{id: worksmacstudio..., weight:2}], worker_count:1}. skeleton_drafts: {worker_count:2, requested:1, ...} — same key, same run, two different quantities. Max observed task concurrency in the log is 2 (depth-2 for 2738s), matching weight, not pool_resolved.worker_count.
n1-r0.mechanism: Two emitters serialize different concepts (physical devices vs weight-derived slots) under one field name, so any offline analysis joining on worker_count — including occupancy or per-worker throughput math across the run archive — silently mixes units.
n1-r0.fix_direction: Rename one field (e.g. device_count vs slot_count) or emit both explicitly in each event; add a replay test asserting the two events agree on the same quantity.

n1-r0.title: Retries/stalls/fallbacks: clean — but only because every failure path stayed untested
n1-r0.evidence: 15/15 tasks completed with attempts=1, status='done', salvaged=false, error=null; 0 detail_fallback, 0 skeleton_failed, 0 complete_stall_exit, 0 run_resumed, 0 kind mismatches (all rules_delivered kinds match task shape: 5 implementer, 6 read-only-shard, 2 test-author tailored=true, 1 owns-nothing, 1 test-author). In-session tool errors were absorbed without retry: api 3 not-ok tool calls, web 1, verify::web 2, test-python-modules 2, verify-e2e::1 1. Worker levers worker_timeout_secs=420 and progress_watchdog_secs=900 never fired despite test-python-modules running 1523s and web going 392s without an owned-file write.
n1-r0.mechanism: The retry/salvage machinery cost nothing this run, which is the good case — but the 420s worker timeout demonstrably does not bound task wall time (1523s at attempts=1), so it is a per-turn or reset-on-activity timer, and the 900s progress watchdog keys on writes that shell-heavy phases (long pytest runs) keep refreshing; neither lever constrains the long-pole behavior documented in the fat-task finding.
n1-r0.fix_direction: No defect to fix in the retry path itself; document/rename worker_timeout_secs to reflect its actual per-turn semantics so wall-time expectations (and the 420s 'floor' referenced in judge tuning comments) are not read as a task cap it does not enforce.

n1-r1.title: Semantic judge structurally unreachable on 1 node: 78/78 LLM reviews skipped, supervision reduced to one deterministic accept in 97 min
n1-r1.evidence: 79 judge_observed, 79 judge_verdict, 78 judge_skipped with reason=no_idle_device (100% of skip events). The 78 non-deterministic verdicts are all verdict=ok, action=observed, confidence=1.0, hint="" — a constant confidence carrying zero signal. The only verdict that acted is 1 deterministic accept (test-meridian, 07:02:54Z). 0 nudges (lever judge_nudge=false), 0 kills, 0 splits. Crucially, 15 of the 78 skips fired between t+4062.9s and t+5047.8s — a window when a device slot demonstrably WAS free, but it was consumed by three pre_review jobs (459s+234s+202s), so the spiralling worker (test-meridian, thinking_chars 14650, three 300-454s write gaps) got zero semantic reviews exactly when it needed one.
n1-r1.mechanism: swarm.rs:20728 — judge_model_id is only granted when a device has in_flight < weight; on a 1-node pool the fleet is saturated whenever a task runs, and the idle-slot fallback (pre_review) competes for and wins the same spare slot. omni_judge=true is dead weight on single-node runs.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Arbitrate the idle slot by need: a worker in a measured think-spiral (tool_calls frozen, thinking growing, no writes for >N s) should outrank a speculative pre_review for the free slot. Alternatively, on worker_count==1 pools, disable the semantic-review machinery explicitly and tighten deterministic thresholds instead of logging 78 no-op verdicts.

n1-r1.title: test-meridian burned 1571s (longest task, 41% of the execute tail) on 6 tool calls with three 300-454s think-only stalls, was accepted stale, and its deliverable failed the complete gate 0.8s later
n1-r1.evidence: Dispatched t+3476.3s, judge-accepted t+5047.8s (elapsed_ms=1571425). judge_observed trail: tool count frozen at 6 from t+4612s, thinking_chars frozen at 14650 from t+4800.6s (247s fully dead — no tools, no thinking, no writes), secs_since_last_write climbing 19→454. Accept hint: 'All 1 owned file(s) exist and pass their syntax check, and nothing has changed for 454s — the deliverable is complete.' At t+5048.6s complete_verify round 0: findings=1 — pytest FAILED tests/test_meridian.py, the exact file this task owned — triggering a 767s serial complete-fix. Producing-then-repairing this one file cost 2338s, ~40% of the 5864s run.
n1-r1.mechanism: The deterministic accept (judge.rs:554-580) requires only file-exists + syntax-passes + 420s stale; it has no functional check, so a wrong test file is accepted as 'complete' and the cost re-materialises in the gate phase. The 420s stale clock also keys on writes alone, so a provably dead session (thinking AND tools frozen) still waits out the full window.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Before accepting a test-author's file, run a cheap functional probe (pytest --collect-only or execute the file) — the complete gate runs the same check seconds later anyway. Add a dead-session fast-path: thinking_chars AND tool_calls unchanged across N consecutive observations → accept/kill immediately (here ~250s of the wait was provably dead).

n1-r1.title: Verification outspent implementation ~2.3:1 yet no gate ever exercised POST /api/sync — the endpoint every lost B-tier point traces to
n1-r1.evidence: Task-time split from task_completed: implementers (main/api/store/meridian/web) 2303.1s vs verify shards+e2e+sink 1496.3s + test-author tasks 2800.9s + pre_review 1004s + gate phase 768s (12.8 min). spec_contract rounds 0 AND 1 both log probed_post=0, inconclusive=1, reason: 'POST /api/sync ... NOT probed because this check only issues bare GETs'. Final state: complete_result passed=true verified=false remaining_findings=0, review new_findings=[]. The sb4 grader then measured sync_completeness 25/247 (0.10), resync_idempotent 0.0, total_field 0.0, summary_accuracy 0.0. The plan's own meridian spec even ordered 'Tests must verify: Pagination: returns all payments' — and the suite that passed round 1 verified it only against mocks. (The app defect itself is F823/F824, out of scope; this finding is the gate blind spot that let it ship green.)
n1-r1.mechanism: spec_contract is GET-only by design; model-authored tests mock the vendor; verify::*/e2e shards raised zero findings; so the entire 5.3-node-hours of verification had structurally zero coverage of the one mutating endpoint, and 'verified' can never be true for any spec advertising a POST.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Extend spec_contract to issue one safe POST to advertised mutating endpoints, or add a deterministic cross-check the run already has the data for: after POST /api/sync, compare /api/summary count against the vendor's total (both reachable from the gate harness).

n1-r1.title: Pre-review findings were mostly unconsumable: the sink dispatched 1063s before the first pre-review finished, and the only had_findings=true result has no downstream consumer event
n1-r1.evidence: integrate-verify (the M5-intended consumer) dispatched t+3459.2s. pre_review completions: api t+4522.0s (had_findings=TRUE, 459s), meridian t+4755.6s (false, 234s), test-store t+4957.7s (false, 202s), test-api t+5066.9s (false, 109s). Injection happens at dispatch time only (swarm.rs:24432 read_prereview_findings into owns-nothing/sink prompts); the last dispatch of the run was complete-fix at t+5048.6s, so test-api's 109s pre-review finished 18.3s after the final possible consumer and was read by nothing. The api findings appear in no later event: complete-fix's baseline_findings=1 (the pytest failure only), final review shows new_findings=[] and pre_existing_skipped=0.
n1-r1.mechanism: Pre-review runs on idle slots; on a 1-node run slots only go idle AFTER the sink has dispatched, so dispatch-time prompt injection structurally misses. 1004s of node time produced findings with no verifiable consumer.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Either hold sink dispatch until in-flight pre-reviews land, or feed late pre-review findings into the next complete_verify round as baseline findings instead of dispatch-time prompt injection.

n1-r1.title: 21.4% of wall is a serial planning prologue; dep-free implementers waited 331-391s after their own specs were ready
n1-r1.evidence: run_started t+0 → first task_dispatched t+1255.2s. Breakdown: research 353.9s, skeleton_drafts 153s (best-of-2 clamped to 1: requested_best_of_n=2, requested=1, clamped=true), 9 detail_completed totalling 1297 model-secs between t+621.6 and t+1157.2, contracts+plan_loaded t+1255.1. run_finished phases confirm: research_min 5.9 + planning_min 15.0 of total_min 97.0. api's detail completed t+864.4 and main's t+923.0, but both dispatched only at t+1255.2 — blocked behind detailing of the four test-* tasks and contract freeze.
n1-r1.mechanism: The detail phase details all 17 tasks (including test tasks that cannot run until their targets exist) before releasing any dispatch; nothing overlaps planning with execution on a 1-node pool.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Release dep-free implementer tasks as soon as their own detail+contract are frozen; detail test-author tasks concurrently with early execution — they are never dispatchable first anyway (all have deps).

n1-r1.title: Judge-accepted tasks corrupt per-task telemetry: task_completed records tool_calls=[] and session_id=null while judge_observed saw 6 tool calls
n1-r1.evidence: test-meridian task_completed (seq 308): status=done, salvaged=false, tool_calls=[], session_id=null — but judge_observed at t+5047.8s for the same task records tools=6, and 16 other completions all carry full tool lists. Any tool-usage or fetched_external aggregation over task_completed under-counts every accept-path task.
n1-r1.mechanism: scheduler.rs:1942+ — the accept path aborts the worker and synthesizes the completion without the session digest. The sibling defect on this exact path (elapsed_ms hard-coded 0) was already found and fixed per the comment at scheduler.rs:1916; tool_calls and session_id were left behind.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Carry the last judge_observed tool count (or a digest snapshot captured at abort) into the synthesized completion, exactly as was done for elapsed_ms.

n1-r1.title: Contract validation failed on module 'main' (invalid syntax) and the pipeline froze contracts anyway with no retry or flag
n1-r1.evidence: contracts event t+1255.1s: frozen=true, injected=3 with injected_modules=[api, meridian, store]; validated.modules includes main: {bytes: 90, parsed: false, error: 'invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?'}. No regeneration, retry, or warning event follows anywhere in the log — main's contract was silently dropped from injection.
n1-r1.mechanism: Contract freeze does not require all modules to parse; a parse failure just excludes that module from injection. Harmless this run (main was 'easy' and completed clean in 176s), but the validation is note-and-ignore: the one gate that checked the artifact found it broken and nothing acted.
n1-r1.fix_direction: One bounded regeneration attempt for a module whose contract fails to parse, or emit it as a first-class finding so a coverage drop is visible instead of silent.

n1-r1.title: Availability machinery all idle (clean, but confirms the failure axis) and the overview ships an unverified run command
n1-r1.evidence: All 17 tasks completed status=done on attempt 1 (attempts=1 in all 17 task_completed; max_attempts=3, retarget_rounds=4 configured); 0 retries, 0 transient errors, 0 salvages (salvaged=false x17), 0 kills, 0 kind-mismatch events; rules_delivered 18 = 17 tasks + complete-fix with kinds consistent (5 implementer, 7 read-only-shard, 4 test-author tailored=true, 2 owns-nothing). Meanwhile run_overview: generated=true but run_command_verified=false for 'python3 -m vendorsync --help', and complete_result verified=false — the run ends with both of its outward claims ('here is how to run it', 'it passed') formally unestablished.
n1-r1.mechanism: Every reliability counter this log can fire stayed at zero — the run's losses came entirely from the unsupervised-quality dimension (findings 1-3), not availability. The overview generator spends 47s (t+5817.2→5864.2) writing a run command it never executes.
n1-r1.fix_direction: Execute the overview's run_command once before writing it (the harness is already in the built tree); treat verified=false at complete_result as a signal to surface, not just log — e.g. print the inconclusive reason into the final report the way the gate phase already does on stderr.

n3-r1.title: Completion gate passes on 'inconclusive' while the test suite hangs and the failing surface goes unprobed
n3-r1.evidence: complete_verify (seq 297, t=4762s): {passed: true, findings: 0} with inconclusive_reasons: ["`pytest -q` did not complete (missing or timed out at 120s)", "spec-contract: probed 3 GET endpoints; POST /api/sync NOT probed"]. spec_contract: probed_post=0. complete_result: {passed: true, verified: false, remaining_findings: 0}. complete_cap_lifted provisioned rounds=2 but only round 0 ran (findings=0 so no fix round). Reproduced the pytest hang in the snapshot dir: 29 tests collected, suite freezes at test 13, test_meridian.py::test_fetch_all_429_retry_after_http_date — it feeds a mocked 429 with hardcoded `Retry-After: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT` and vendorsync/meridian.py:40-41,58 does `delta=(dt-now).total_seconds(); time.sleep(max(0.5,delta))` = a real ~67-day sleep on 2026-08-15; 16 of 29 tests (all of test_store.py) never ran. Graded outcome: tier B mean 0.349 with sync_completeness 0/247 — exactly the POST /api/sync surface that was never probed. pre_review of test-meridian (438s, t=3984) had_findings=false on the file containing the sleeping test. run_overview: run_command_verified=false.
n3-r1.mechanism: The verify round only converts explicit findings into fix rounds; inconclusive checks (hung pytest, unprobed POST endpoint) are logged as strings and then treated as pass. The test author mocked urlopen but not time.sleep, so a wall-clock-dependent retry test hangs the whole suite, and nothing in the pipeline (pre_review, judge accept-on-syntax-check, complete_verify) ever ran or diagnosed it.
n3-r1.fix_direction: Make each inconclusive_reason a blocking finding that triggers the already-provisioned round 1 (cap was lifted to 3000s for 2 rounds and never used): re-run pytest with a per-test timeout to name the hanging test, and probe advertised POST endpoints with a benign body instead of skipping them. In test-author rules, require sleep/time to be mocked whenever retry logic is under test.

n3-r1.title: Judge-accept path discards the work it accepts — 3 of 4 e2e shards and test-meridian contribute empty results
n3-r1.evidence: task_completed for verify-e2e::1 (t=3801s), ::2 (t=3891s), ::3 (t=3966s) and test-meridian (t=3545s): all status=done, attempts=2, session_id=None, tool_calls=[] (4 of 20 completions = 20%). Yet judge_observed at the same instants counted 11, 8, and 9 tool calls in the observed e2e sessions, and the accept hints say "has taken 11/8/9 action(s)... take what it established as the result". run_finished results for verify-e2e::1/2/3 and test-meridian are empty strings, while verify-e2e::0 (completed normally) carries a full golden-check report. The e2e join spanned 2525→3966s = 1441s = 29.9% of the wall and delivered exactly one shard's worth of verification into integrate-verify.
n3-r1.mechanism: When a task is closed by deterministic accept instead of by the agent finishing, the completion record is synthesized without harvesting the session: session_id, tool_calls, and the result text are all dropped. The 'establishment' the accept verdict cites is never persisted, so the sink receives nothing from those shards, and the log contradicts itself (judge counts 8-11 actions, completion records zero).
n3-r1.fix_direction: On accept, harvest the observed session's last assistant message and tool-call list into the completion record (the judge_observed event already has a handle on the session). A join whose shards can be accept-closed must carry the shard transcript forward, otherwise fan_e2e is paying 30% of the wall for one shard of output.

n3-r1.title: LLM judge is a 62x 'ok' rubber stamp; every intervention that worked was deterministic
n3-r1.evidence: 71 judge_verdict events: 62 'ok' (all deterministic=false, i.e. LLM calls) with hint='' every time; 13 of 14 verdicts on test-meridian were 'ok' while the observed agent was frozen — thinking_chars pinned at the same value across up to 6 consecutive observations (1108 chars at t=2403-2675, 1198 at t=2736-3056), tool_calls stuck at 1-2 for 874s, secs_since_last_write climbing to 879. The stall was caught not by the judge but by the separate 420s watchdog (task_retry t=3114, 'no progress for 420s'). The 6 deterministic verdicts did all the useful work: 2 act-now nudges at t=1492 (meridian: 0 files, 7656 chars reasoning after 7.3 min; web: 0 files, 1 command) and 4 accepts. Additionally 49 of 120 judge cycles (40.8%) were judge_skipped reason=no_idle_device.
n3-r1.mechanism: The LLM judge only emits a hint when re-dispatching; an 'ok' carries zero information and no nudge, so 95% of LLM judge inference (62/65 calls) produced no signal, while the stall signature it repeatedly observed (identical thinking_chars, zero new tool calls) is a trivially deterministic predicate it never acted on. Judge capacity is also gated on an idle device, so it starves exactly when the swarm is saturated.
n3-r1.fix_direction: Add the frozen-telemetry predicate (thinking_chars and tool_calls unchanged across N observations) to the deterministic rule set so it nudges/kills without an LLM call, and skip the LLM verdict entirely when observed features are unchanged since the last 'ok' — that removes most of the 62 no-op calls and frees the idle-device budget the 49 skips were starved of.

n3-r1.title: Judge re-dispatch of read-only e2e shards backfires: accurate diagnoses thrown away, replacements stall to the 420s threshold
n3-r1.evidence: Three LLM re_dispatch verdicts killed e2e shard attempt 0 after 800/749/736s: t=3370 verify-e2e::1 spec_drift ('server isn't running, connection refused on port 18890'), t=3470 verify-e2e::2 broken_code ('vendorsync/api.py handler crashes during request handling'), t=3545 verify-e2e::3 broken_code ('store.py IndentationError line 32; __main__.py line 6 incomplete import'). The replacement attempts ran exactly 430/421/420s and were then deterministically accepted with 'done nothing new for a while'; their completion records are empty (see finding 2). test-meridian shows the same shape: attempt 1 after the watchdog retry ran 431s with 0 tool calls and 117 thinking chars before accept — the accepted artifact was attempt 0's file, already unchanged for 879s when the retry was even launched (written t≈2667, retry launched t=3114).
n3-r1.mechanism: For a read-only verification shard, restarting the shard cannot fix the broken code it diagnosed; the diagnosis lives only in the discarded hint while the fresh agent re-derives the same dead end and trips the same 420s inactivity threshold. For test-meridian, retry fired on an agent whose deliverable was already complete and stable — the accept criterion (file exists, syntax-clean, unchanged) was satisfiable 448s before the retry started.
n3-r1.fix_direction: Route broken_code/spec_drift hints from read-only shards to the sink (integrate-verify) or a fix task instead of re-dispatching the shard; evaluate the deterministic accept predicate before spending a retry attempt. Net measured waste: ~1,700 device-seconds of replacement attempts plus three discarded shard establishments.

n3-r1.title: Wall anatomy: code-producing work gets ~30% of the run; tail runs 2 of 3 nodes idle for ~17 minutes
n3-r1.evidence: Wall 4822s. Phase shares: run_started→first task_dispatched = 1052s (21.8%, research 406s + skeleton 256s + contracts/detail to 1052s); e2e join 2525→3966s = 1441s (29.9%, yielding one non-empty shard result); sink integrate-verify 3966→4641s = 675s on a single device; final verify+review+overview 4641→4822s = 181s. During the 856s tail, mihai is idle from t=3801 (1021s) and gabee from t=3984 (838s) — ~2,040 idle device-seconds while one node integrates. Reconstructed busy intervals also show gabee at the lowest utilization (its only post-1943s work was the stalled test-meridian pair and one pre-review). First-attempt losses compound it: meridian and web each burned 440s (t=1052→1492) producing zero owned files before the act-now nudge fired.
n3-r1.mechanism: The pipeline is phase-serial at both ends — nothing dispatches until detailing finishes, and the sink plus final verify are single-threaded — so a 3-node swarm spends the first fifth planning and the last sixth with two nodes parked, while the middle third is the e2e join that mostly evaporated (finding 2).
n3-r1.fix_direction: Overlap the tail: let the idle nodes run the final-verify probes (spec-contract GETs, pytest, http_timeout_scan) concurrently with the sink's integration edits, and start easy tasks whose specs are already detailed instead of gating all dispatch on the full detail phase.

n3-r1.title: Contract validation failures silently downgrade to no-contract: api and web frozen unparsed, no retry
n3-r1.evidence: contracts event (t=1052s): frozen=true, modules=5, injected=3 (meridian, store, cli). Module api: parsed=false, error='unterminated triple-quoted string literal' (364 bytes); module web: parsed=false, error='invalid syntax. Perhaps you forgot a comma?' (79 bytes). Levers: contract_validate=true but contract_retry=false. No later event repairs or re-freezes them; the api and web tasks were dispatched with no injected contract. The graded run's failures concentrate in the API surface (tier B mean 0.349), though the root cause there is the out-of-scope sync defect.
n3-r1.mechanism: contract_validate detects the malformed contract at freeze time but with contract_retry off there is no repair path, so a 2/5 contract-authoring failure is logged and swallowed — the freeze proceeds and the affected modules simply lose contract injection, unannounced to any downstream consumer.
n3-r1.fix_direction: On parsed=false, spend one bounded regeneration attempt (the contract_retry lever already exists) or at minimum surface the failure as a finding to the sink; a contract that fails to parse should never freeze silently as 'no contract'.

n3-r1.title: pre_review consumed 1,843 device-seconds with no consumer for its one finding
n3-r1.evidence: 9 pre_review events totaling 1,843s of device time (individual: store 293s, test-store 177s, cli 127s, api 219s, readme 133s, test-api 159s, meridian 214s, web 83s, test-meridian 438s). had_findings=true exactly once (store, t=1724s); the run dispatched 26 task attempts and none is a fix task — lever fix_sched=false — so the finding had no downstream consumer, and store was never re-dispatched. The 438s review of test-meridian returned had_findings=false on the file whose hardcoded-date test hangs the whole suite (finding 1).
n3-r1.mechanism: The review stage runs unconditionally per task but its output only matters if a fix scheduler exists; with fix_sched off, had_findings=true is a dead-end boolean, making the entire stage cost with zero possible effect on the artifact.
n3-r1.fix_direction: Either wire pre_review findings into the sink's work queue (it runs later and does edit files) or skip pre_review when fix_sched is off; and give test-file reviews a concrete checklist item for unmocked sleep/wall-clock dependencies, which this 438s review missed.

n3-r1.title: Telemetry contradictions: kind=None on all 26 dispatches, zero kind_mismatch events, unverified run command
n3-r1.evidence: All 26 task_dispatched events log kind=None even though kind_prompt=true and rules_delivered proves kind-specific selection happened (rules_sections: read-only-shard x13, test-author x4, owns-nothing x1, generic x8; tailored=true on only 4 of 26). kind_mismatch events: 0 in the entire log. task_completed for accept-closed tasks contradicts judge_observed on the same task at the same second (tool_calls=[] vs 11/8/9 observed — detailed in finding 2). run_overview: run_command_verified=false on the shipped README command.
n3-r1.mechanism: The kind classification is computed and used for rules delivery but never written back into the dispatch event, so any analysis keying on dispatched kind (including kind_mismatch detection, which fired zero times) is blind — a mismatch could not have been recorded even if it occurred.
n3-r1.fix_direction: Populate task_dispatched.kind from the same value that selected rules_sections, and emit the accept-path completion from the observed session so the two event streams cannot disagree; verify the run_overview command with one bounded execution before writing it into the report.
